se-apocryphal-1.explanation: A story with no trace in any record from the time is widely told and probably untrue, which apocryphal and spurious both say; the others describe its age or style instead.
se-apocryphal-1.stem: The story of the founder sleeping in the workshop for a year is _____: it appears in no letter, ledger or photograph from the period.

se-apostate-1.explanation: Going from chief defender to a name struck off the masthead is abandoning the cause, which apostate and renegade both say; the other four are words for staying loyal.
se-apostate-1.stem: Once the doctrine's most quoted defender, he became after the pamphlet the movement's most cited _____, his name struck from the journal's masthead.

se-chary-1.explanation: Having been cheated twice produces caution, not trust or haste, and chary and wary both leave the buyer equally guarded about paying in advance; credulous and gullible get the lesson backwards.
se-chary-1.stem: Burned twice by suppliers who vanished after the deposit cleared, the buyer grew _____ of any firm that asked for money before delivery.

se-desultory-1.explanation: A box here, a box there and corners untouched is a search with no method, which desultory and haphazard both name and the other four contradict.
se-desultory-1.stem: Their search of the attic was _____: one box opened here, another there, and whole corners never looked into at all.

se-grandiloquent-1.explanation: Laughter at the solemn part follows from language inflated past what the occasion carries, and grandiloquent and bombastic both leave the speech pompous.
se-grandiloquent-1.stem: His acceptance speech was so _____ that the audience laughed aloud at a passage he had clearly intended as its solemn heart.

se-lethargic-1.explanation: Abandoning the quota and sending workers home follows from a shift with no energy left in it, and lethargic and torpid both leave the afternoon equally sluggish; ebullient and vivacious supply the energy it lacked.
se-lethargic-1.stem: The heat left the whole afternoon shift _____; by two o'clock the supervisor had given up on the quota and sent half the floor home.

se-opprobrium-1.explanation: What follows a verdict and ruins a quiet retirement is public disgrace, and opprobrium and obloquy both leave him condemned; acclaim and deference would be the reverse.
se-opprobrium-1.stem: The verdict brought him not the quiet retirement he had planned for but years of public _____, in the papers and on every doorstep he passed.

se-pellucid-1.explanation: An untrained reader following every step is the test the sentence sets, and pellucid and limpid both make the writing perfectly clear; the others make it harder to read.
se-pellucid-1.stem: After three rewrites the explanation had become _____, and a reader with no training in the field could follow every step of the argument.

se-pervasive-1.explanation: The same mark in every flat on every floor rules out the occasional, which is all sporadic and intermittent offer, and pervasive and ubiquitous both spread the damp through the whole block.
se-pervasive-1.stem: Damp in that block is _____: every flat on every floor shows the same brown line a hand's width above the skirting board.

se-quotidian-1.explanation: Weighing, labelling and copying the same column is routine set against the thrill she expected, and quotidian and humdrum both leave the work ordinary.
se-quotidian-1.stem: She had expected the laboratory to be thrilling and found the work _____: weighing samples, labelling tubes, copying the same numbers into the same column.

se-refractory-1.explanation: Three courses of treatment changing nothing is resistance to control, which refractory and recalcitrant both name; transient and transitory would have it clearing on its own, and virulent describes severity.
se-refractory-1.stem: The infection proved _____: three full courses of the standard antibiotic left the counts exactly where they had been at the start.

se-tyro-1.explanation: Losing four straight hands to players who saw through him immediately marks a beginner, and tyro and neophyte both leave him new to the game.
se-tyro-1.stem: For all his confidence at the table, he was a _____ at the game and lost the first four hands to players who had read him at once.

tc-abeyance-1.explanation: Not repealed, suspended for now, and restorable by one vote is exactly temporary suspension, which abeyance names; dissolution would end the rule for good.
tc-abeyance-1.stem: The rule has not been repealed but held in _____ while the review runs, and a single vote of the committee can bring it back.

tc-abscond-1.explanation: Leaving with the money to avoid an audit and turning up abroad is fleeing in secret, which abscond means; capitulate and acquiesce would mean facing it.
tc-abscond-1.stem: The treasurer chose to _____ with the quarter's takings rather than face the audit, and was traced six months later to another country.

tc-anodyne-1.explanation: Wording no faction can object to is chosen to give no offence, which is anodyne; polemical and contentious would invite the argument it avoids.
tc-anodyne-1.stem: The statement was deliberately _____: three paragraphs that no faction could object to and that committed the company to nothing whatever.

tc-approbation-1.explanation: Three committees passing it unamended and a friendly notice in the paper is broad approval, which approbation names; censure and derision would be the opposite.
tc-approbation-1.stem: The design met with general _____: three committees passed it without amendment and even the local paper called it long overdue.

tc-arrogate-1.explanation: Taking a power the charter never granted is claiming it without right, which arrogate means; relinquish, cede and forfeit all give power away instead.
tc-arrogate-1.stem: No clause in the charter allowed the chairman to _____ the power of appointing trustees, yet he had quietly been doing so for a decade.

tc-aver-1.explanation: Sticking to the same claim after the footage is played is stating it confidently as fact, which aver means; recant and retract would abandon it.
tc-aver-1.stem: The defendant continued to _____ that he had never entered the building, even after the footage was played twice in open court.

tc-benign-1.explanation: Needing nothing beyond a check-up in a year means the growth does no harm, which is benign; the other four all make it dangerous in one way or another.
tc-benign-1.stem: The growth turned out to be _____, and the surgeon told her she would need nothing beyond a routine check-up in a year's time.

tc-brook-1.explanation: Stopping the orchestra at the first whisper shows she allows no talking at all, and brook is the verb for tolerating that the sentence negates.
tc-brook-1.stem: A conductor of the old school, she would _____ no talking during rehearsal and stopped the orchestra at the first whisper from the back desks.

tc-candid-1.explanation: Naming sums and dates unprompted, set against the hedging of the others, is straightforward honesty, which candid supplies and evasive and reticent deny.
tc-candid-1.stem: Most of the witnesses hedged, but one was unexpectedly _____, naming the sums and the dates without once being pressed to do so.

tc-catalyst-1.explanation: The wage cut comes before the walkout and sets it off, so the blank needs the thing that triggers change; catalyst says that, while corollary and upshot are results.
tc-catalyst-1.stem: The strike had been building for years; the wage cut announced in March was merely the _____ that turned a standing grievance into a walkout.

tc-cupidity-1.explanation: Mortgaging the second estate to buy a third while needing nothing is greed for wealth, which cupidity names and frugality and temperance contradict.
tc-cupidity-1.stem: What the letters record is not need but _____: he already held two estates and was mortgaging the second in order to buy a third.

tc-dilatory-1.explanation: A fortnight to answer each question, adding weeks to the job, is delay rather than tone or length, which is what dilatory describes.
tc-dilatory-1.stem: The contractor's _____ replies added six weeks to a job of four: every question sent to him took a fortnight to come back answered.

tc-eccentric-1.explanation: The sentence rules out difficult and offers odd habits instead, so the blank is unconventional without being unpleasant, which is eccentric.
tc-eccentric-1.stem: Colleagues found him _____ rather than difficult: he kept a barometer on his desk and would answer only questions put to him in writing.

tc-empirical-1.explanation: Measurements taken in the field and repeatable by anyone is evidence from observation rather than theory, which is what empirical names.
tc-empirical-1.stem: The committee wanted _____ support for the claim rather than another model: measurements from the field, taken under conditions anyone could repeat.

tc-fecund-1.explanation: Two or three crops a year from the same ground is exceptional fertility, which fecund names; dormant would mean nothing grows at all.
tc-fecund-1.stem: The delta soil is so _____ that two crops in a year are ordinary there and a third is not thought remarkable.

tc-garrulous-1.explanation: Forty minutes of the neighbours' business in exchange for buying a newspaper is excessive talk about trivia, which garrulous names; taciturn and laconic mean the reverse.
tc-garrulous-1.stem: Nobody stood beside the _____ shopkeeper twice: an errand for a newspaper cost you forty minutes of his neighbours' business.

tc-hoary-1.explanation: An audience that can mouth the punchline has heard the joke many times before, so it is old and stale, which hoary says.
tc-hoary-1.stem: He opened with the _____ joke about economists and forecasts, and half the audience mouthed the punchline along with him.

tc-imperturbable-1.explanation: Failed engines and a shouting cabin are exactly the conditions that should rattle her, and the voice does not, which is what imperturbable describes.
tc-imperturbable-1.stem: Two engines had failed and the cabin was shouting, but the captain's voice over the intercom remained _____, as though she were reading out a weather report.

tc-impetuous-1.explanation: Resigning mid-meeting before hearing the answer, and regretting it within hours, is acting rashly without thought, which is what impetuous names.
tc-impetuous-1.stem: She resigned in the middle of the meeting, before anyone had answered her question, a decision so _____ that she regretted it before lunch.

tc-inimical-1.explanation: Wind stripping the soil so that nothing can stand upright makes the ridge actively hostile to plants, which is what inimical says; idyllic and serene say the reverse.
tc-inimical-1.stem: Conditions on the ridge are _____ to anything with roots: the wind strips the soil away and whatever survives lies flat against the rock.

tc-languid-1.explanation: Waiters crossing a terrace so slowly that the dogs will not even rise for them sets the pace as slow and without energy, which is what languid means.
tc-languid-1.stem: Nothing in the afternoon heat moved quickly: the waiters crossed the terrace so _____ that the dogs watching them did not bother to get up at all.

tc-lugubrious-1.explanation: Turning a drinking song into a funeral march is making it mournful, which lugubrious names; ebullient and sanguine would keep it cheerful.
tc-lugubrious-1.stem: The band's _____ arrangement turned a cheerful drinking song into something much closer to a funeral march.

tc-malevolent-1.explanation: The sentence contrasts the blank with haste and bad records by ruling out a wish to hurt anyone, so the missing motive is the malevolent one.
tc-malevolent-1.stem: Nothing in the file suggests the motive was _____; the damage came from haste and poor record-keeping rather than from any wish to hurt the family.

tc-mendicant-1.explanation: Owning nothing and living on what villages give is begging under a religious vow, which is what a mendicant is; a magnate or potentate would own a great deal.
tc-mendicant-1.stem: Sworn to own nothing at all, each brother took to the road as the order's _____, living on whatever the villages along it would give him.

tc-mercurial-1.explanation: Unexplained swings between praise and silence are sudden, unpredictable changes of mood, which is what mercurial names; adamant would mean he never shifted at all.
tc-mercurial-1.stem: Praise on Monday and silence on Tuesday, with nothing in between to explain the change: his staff learned to treat his _____ temper as weather rather than judgement.

tc-mundane-1.explanation: Expense claims and an unringing telephone are the ordinary and unexciting side of the job, which is what mundane names; arduous would make it hard rather than dull.
tc-mundane-1.stem: For all the talk of espionage, most of the work was _____: filing expense claims, booking flights, and waiting for a telephone that rarely rang.

tc-nuance-1.explanation: Three kinds of obligation flattened into one word is a loss of fine distinctions, which is what nuance means; a platitude or tautology would be no loss at all.
tc-nuance-1.stem: Translated word for word, the speech loses every _____: the original distinguishes three kinds of obligation where the English has only duty.

tc-obviate-1.explanation: A sensor that makes the nightly inspection unnecessary removes the need for it rather than arguing against it, and obviate is the word for that.
tc-obviate-1.stem: One well-placed sensor would _____ the nightly inspection that currently costs four hours and two members of staff.

tc-partisan-1.explanation: Reading as a brief for one side is exactly the failure of neutrality the sentence sets up, which partisan names and dispassionate denies.
tc-partisan-1.stem: The inquiry was meant to be neutral, yet its final chapter is so _____ that it reads as a brief for one side rather than a finding of fact.

tc-perennial-1.explanation: A complaint recorded in 1890 and in every year since is one that keeps recurring, which perennial says; transient and ephemeral would make it brief.
tc-perennial-1.stem: Flooding on that road is the _____ complaint of the parish: it appears in the minutes of 1890 and in every set of minutes taken since.

tc-precipitate-1.explanation: One sentence that sets off a bank run has caused it suddenly, which is what precipitate means; avert would mean the run never happened.
tc-precipitate-1.stem: A single sentence in the governor's speech was enough to _____ a run on the bank that took three weeks and a federal loan to stop.

tc-pristine-1.explanation: Two centuries sealed away with the ink still black says the manuscript was untouched and unspoiled, which is pristine; dilapidated would be the opposite.
tc-pristine-1.stem: The manuscript had lain in a sealed chest for two centuries and came out _____, its ink still as black as the day it dried.

tc-probity-1.explanation: A reputation that survives accusations of wrongdoing is one for uprightness rather than mere frankness, and probity is the word for that integrity.
tc-probity-1.stem: Thirty years on the bench had earned him a reputation for _____ that survived even the accusations made by his last opponent.

tc-proliferate-1.explanation: Three brands becoming forty in two years is a rapid increase in number, which proliferate names; abate, wane and ebb all move the other way.
tc-proliferate-1.stem: Once the patent lapsed, cheap copies began to _____, and within two years the shelves carried forty brands where there had been three.

tc-reprobate-1.explanation: Unpaid debts, broken promises and abandoned engagements describe a man without principles, which reprobate names and paragon reverses.
tc-reprobate-1.stem: His brother is spoken of in the family as the _____ of his generation: debts unpaid, promises broken, and two engagements abandoned without explanation.

tc-sanction-1.explanation: A board withholding approval of a merger pending a review is deciding whether to authorise it, which is the sense sanction carries here.
tc-sanction-1.stem: The board declined to _____ the merger until the regulator had finished its own review of the two pension schemes.

tc-sedulous-1.explanation: Twenty years of steady work that ends in the county's only reliable census describes persistent diligence, which sedulous names; cursory and erratic would not have produced it.
tc-sedulous-1.stem: Twenty years of _____ note-taking in parish registers produced the one reliable census of the county that historians still use today.

tc-whimsical-1.explanation: Doors onto walls and giant benches are playful inventions that raise a laugh, which is what whimsical describes.
tc-whimsical-1.stem: The garden was full of _____ touches — a door that opened onto a wall, a bench built for a giant — that made visitors laugh rather than admire.
